PullRequest.Title: sessions: show pending automatic host connections on web
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Keep web `/agents` hosts visibly **Connecting** while automatic connection setup is still in progress, even after discovery finishes and before a protocol connection entry exists.

Previously, discovery could finish and the indicator turn idle while transport setup continued. The passive indicator and modal host summary now reflect actual pending setup, and captured diagnostics include the attempt's start time, elapsed time, automatic/manual trigger, and whether a protocol connection entry exists.

On phones, Connection Information is also accessible beside the **Hosts** sheet title. Opening it dismisses the picker first; closing the report restores the originating control, or its workbench toolbar if the control was replaced while the host connected.

## Implementation and boundaries

- Expose actual in-flight attempts through a read-only catalog and dedicated invalidation event, rather than inferring activity from discovery or historical log events.
- Preserve established, reconnecting, and incompatible states. Completed attempts clear by identity; removed, disabled, and disposed hosts are excluded from the catalog.
- Preserve connection scheduling, retry policy, and native UI status behavior. The connection indicator remains passive.
- Rebased onto main including #336443. Pending state now coexists with its asynchronous snapshot capture, connection-stage history, and Window-log excerpt. Tests verify that a historical start event does not keep a completed attempt marked pending.
- Tighten notification regression tests, use one numeric snapshot timestamp for elapsed calculations, and document the pending-state contract.

## Product validation

Used standalone Chromium against the local `/agents` build with deliberately delayed mock transport setup. Desktop and phone-emulated runs verified pending status in the indicator and modal, combined pending/stage/log evidence, Copy/Download equivalence allowing Windows clipboard line endings, and transition to Connected. The phone Hosts-sheet information entry was activated using actual Playwright touch taps.

This uncovered a focus loss when the mobile toolbar replaced the original host control while diagnostics was open. The toolbar fallback now passes both the targeted regression test and the completed desktop/phone-emulated end-to-end rerun, including replacement of the original mobile control. Device emulation is not physical-phone/PWA or real-tunnel validation.

Additional manual-connection validation caught a staging race: clearing suppression before staging could start an automatic dial first. Suppression now clears as part of staging, and the pending catalog reads the factory’s effective initiation mode. Held both automatic and manual attempts pending in Chromium and verified their respective triggers in downloaded diagnostics, equivalent copied evidence, eventual Connected state, and phone touch/focus recovery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Web startup and first tunnel discovery automatically connect configured or newly discovered hosts while showing pending status
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Factory registration/reconciliation starts existing cached-host dials before the tunnel contribution subscribes; first discovery later caches newly found tunnels and starts their dials. The new pending event synchronously updates provider status, but remote authentication, gateway setup, and protocol connection remain the dominant asynchronous critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per initial or user-triggered rediscovery, serving the full tunnel collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery request and collection-wide response occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery must complete before newly found hosts can be cached and connected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist each newly discovered tunnel into application storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage update per previously uncached discovered tunnel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discovery already cached each new tunnel individually.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs synchronously while applying discovery results before status reconciliation completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticate, establish the tunnel gateway/relay, and perform the agent-host protocol connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active setup per normalized address; up to the number of unsuppressed configured hosts across distinct addresses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-address dials and aggregate cross-address concurrency existed; the PR adds pending metadata/events but no extra dial.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each host cannot become connected until its own setup and protocol handshake finish.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured/cached tunnel count after suppression and dismissal filtering; one deduplicated in-flight attempt per normalized address. Discovery can add multiple hosts, but each address has at most one pending dial.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RemoteAgentHostService coalesces by address in _pendingConnects. Different addresses can still connect concurrently exactly as before the diff; the PR does not add a global limiter or increase per-address concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm startup reads the existing tunnel cache and auto-connects unsuppressed entries. Cold discovery performs one tunnel-list request, then persists newly discovered tunnels; pending metadata is uncached and exists only for each live attempt. Removed, disabled, and disposed entries are filtered from the exposed catalog.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in event and dial cardinality from _connectTo deduplication, constructor ordering, the pending event listener, and cache iteration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tunnel cache size is unbounded, so pending start/configuration events can cause repeated host-list scans during a large discovery. However, these scans are in-memory, status writes are equality-checked observables, startup registration events precede the new contribution listener, and the diff does not introduce the pre-existing per-host network burst. There is insufficient evidence of a concrete user-visible regression at realistic cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR exposes existing in-flight work and adds synchronous status recomputation, but does not increase expensive-boundary cardinality or concurrency, and the remaining in-memory scans are not evidenced as materially costly.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user manually connects or reconnects one tunnel from the host UI or diagnostics report
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action stages the tunnel, RemoteAgentHostService starts or joins the one address-specific attempt, then waitForConnection follows that attempt through gateway and protocol setup. Pending status events update the UI without awaiting additional work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update the cached tunnel and suppression state in application storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One staged cache update for the selected host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same staging cache write occurred; suppression was previously also cleared earlier by callers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire authentication if needed and establish gateway/relay plus protocol connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dial for the selected address because concurrent requests join.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same dial occurred. Moving suppression clearing into staging changes initiation ordering/metadata, not boundary count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The connect action waits for this boundary to produce a connection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected host action; repeated requests for the same address join the existing pending promise.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized/coalesced per normalized address by _pendingConnects; unrelated addresses retain pre-existing independent concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: stageTunnel refreshes the cached tunnel and clears suppression as part of staging. A staged initiation flag is consumed by the first createConnection and then removed, so later automatic attempts are not pinned as user-initiated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from reconnect's _pendingConnects check, stageTunnel consumption, and waitForConnection call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication and gateway latency vary by environment, but the changed code neither duplicates nor newly awaits them.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Pending tracking retains three small metadata fields per already-retained promise and emits start/end UI notifications without adding remote calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and use Connection Information on desktop or from the mobile Hosts sheet
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the report captures one snapshot before rendering. Snapshot capture scans bounded diagnostic buffers and host state, then reads a bounded Window-log excerpt. Subsequent pending-state changes only schedule a live DOM rebuild at the next animation frame; they do not call getSnapshot or reread the log. Copy uses the captured text and download encodes it on explicit action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and filter the Window log excerpt for connection-related lines
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file read per initial open or explicit refresh, independent of host count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The diagnostic command already performed this read; the diff adds a direct mobile Hosts-sheet entry point, so one deliberate tap from that new control now reaches the same single snapshot read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial report display waits for snapshot capture. Live pending status updates are off this boundary and only rerender in-memory state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build snapshot sections/text and optionally encode captured text for download
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One collection-wide serialization per open/refresh; one encoding per explicit download.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Snapshot text construction and download encoding already existed; pending attempts add six small entries only for currently pending hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Snapshot serialization precedes report display; download encoding occurs only on the user's download action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible/cached/configured hosts plus bounded diagnostic history (up to 200 connection and 200 discovery events) and the bounded log excerpt; one modal instance at a time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pending UI invalidations are coalesced to one render per animation frame. Snapshot requests are explicit; request IDs discard stale refresh results, and host actions are serialized by pendingHostId.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The initial snapshot is retained by the report. Live status rereads current in-memory host state, while detailed sections and exports remain on the captured snapshot until explicit refresh. There is no automatic snapshot or negative-cache retry on pending events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from ConnectionDiagnosticsReport.scheduleRender calling render rather than refresh/getSnapshot and from getSnapshot's single collectConnectionLogs call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact log-read latency and report size depend on platform and host count, but the new pending invalidations provably do not repeat snapshot capture, and the newly exposed mobile path performs only the operation explicitly requested by the user.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new mobile entry deliberately invokes existing diagnostics once, while frequent live changes are coalesced and remain in memory.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close mobile Connection Information after its originating host control was replaced
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution checks the originating focused part before snapshot capture and, on modal close, synchronously focuses either the still-connected element or the mobile titlebar/toolbar fallback.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per modal open/close; independent of host count and connection history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active diagnostics modal is guarded by contribution state; no queue or background work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. The fallback closure is cleared with the mobile titlebar disposable lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the explicit focusPart/hasFocus branches and mobile titlebar lifecycle wiring.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; DOM containment and focus operations are constant-sized and user-triggered.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the change adds only constant synchronous focus work on modal open/close.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 17 changed files and all diff pages. Traced pending-attempt lifecycle, startup/discovery and manual connection cardinality, live diagnostics rendering, snapshot/log capture, mobile report access, and focus restoration. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found, and the PR does not itself establish a concrete shipped performance-regression fix suitable for blame recording.
